title: Look for the Others
hook: A deer in the road, and it is not alone.
scene: Last light. A doe is standing in your lane, broadside, doing what they do, which is nothing. Ditch on the right, oncoming lane on the left, and your hands have already decided which one they like.

source.psdp_skill: Skill twelve: driving on rural roads
source.teaching_target: PSDP twelve Animals: do not swerve. Not DOL 4.19 pets. Timeout = swerve.

image_brief.subject: a doe standing broadside in your travel lane, close, filling the next lengths through the mesh at last light
image_brief.foreground: worn black wheel, faded pink dash, coarse mesh; hands not yet yanking; closed dark carrier latched and strapped on the passenger floor (Gracie inside; wheels turning)
image_brief.midground: doe broadside across the asphalt in this lane — not grazing roadside; ditch right, empty oncoming left
image_brief.background: dusk overcast rural two-lane, treeline, last light not full night
image_brief.read: a deer stands broadside in your lane at dusk, close; the ditch and the oncoming lane wait on either side
extra_negatives: no deer grazing on the roadside shoulder
no deer already past or leaping clear
no full night with only headlamps
no second person in the car
no cat loose on the seat

geometry.ego_lane_side: right half of a two-lane rural road
geometry.ego_nose_in_frame: plow points up-frame at the doe already in the lane
geometry.oncoming_position: left half empty; no oncoming vehicle in frame

variation.forced: Act VI wave-1 briefs landed; stills pending review; do not seed

decision: She's in your lane. You can't stop in time.

options.text: Brake straight, stay in the lane, don't swerve
options.result: You brake hard and hold the wheel and hit nothing, or you hit her and keep the car. Either way you're still pointed down the road — and the second one comes out of the ditch three seconds later.

options.text: Swerve left into the oncoming lane
options.result: The worst crashes are people who missed an animal and found a truck. Oncoming finds you first.
Soft shoulder, a ditch, and a Beetle rolling into it. The ditch takes the car the deer never needed.
Your hands did it. That is the whole reason this card exists. The swerve was the decision.

debrief: Don't swerve for an animal — slow down, be prepared to stop, and look for more. Deer travel in groups.
